originality.rationale: Nearest priors compared substantively, not by timestamp: (1) Howe-Lauter (arXiv math/0207101, fetched) proves improved upper bounds on N_q(g) and eight exact N_q(g) values via zeta constraints and covering arguments — a bound theorem, with no fixed small-height y^2=f(x) model census, no orbit-partition logs, no explicit Serre-maximal point lists for these models. (2) Kudo-Harashita (arXiv 1907.00894, fetched) enumerates superspecial (Jacobian is product of supersingular elliptic curves) hyperelliptic curves, applied to genus 4 — a different extremal property and range than Serre-maximal point count for genus 2 over F19/F29. (3) LMFDB abelian varieties over Fq (g=2, q=19 page fetched: 897 isogeny classes listed as bare L-polynomials/isogeny factors) records isogeny classes, not explicit committed small-height models with uniform Frobenius-orbit enumeration logs and validated full rational-point lists; existence of an isogeny class does not supply the model, the point list, or the in-run maximality certificate. (4) LMFDB Genus2/Q covers curves over Q, not finite-field point-count/zeta witnesses (per admission record). (5) Howe-Maisner-Nart-Ritzenthaler classifies principally polarizable genus-2 isogeny classes structurally, not model-by-model maximal witnesses. No prior source records y^2=x^6-x^5-2x^4+2x^3-2x^2-x+1/F19 with 36 points and Weil data (16,102)/Jac 784, nor y^2=x^6-2x^5+x^4+x^3+x^2-2x+1/F29 with 50 points and (20,158)/Jac 1600, together with full validated point lists. Novelty is exactly the regenerated census plus the two certified maximal point lists, as the DRAFT scopes it — no overclaim on bound theorems or database entries.

value.rationale: Headline result judged on its own: two explicit Serre-bound-attaining genus-2 curves (F19 with 36 points, F29 with 50 points) with exact Weil polynomials, zeta functions, Jacobian orders (784=28^2, 1600=40^2), and full validated rational-point lists. Object (genus-2 hyperelliptic curves over small prime fields) and invariant (Serre-maximal point count plus exact zeta/Jacobian data) were motivated before computation by the recognized Serre maximal-curve classification, Howe-Lauter N_q(g) bound-calibration, and Goppa-code curve-selection programs — pre-existing demand, not packaging-created value. Values are not known or mechanically implied: attaining q+1+2*floor(2*sqrt(q)) is a nontrivial exact Diophantine fact per model (most slice cells do not attain it: only 2 of 118 smooth cells are maximal), and the Weil coefficients/Jacobian orders require the F_{p^2} enumeration. A future researcher can reasonably need precisely these citable witnesses (explicit equation + point list + zeta + Jacobian certificate) for bound calibration, Weil-conjecture examples, or code selection. This is a narrow exact invariant of natural objects under the eligibility clause, not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration. The surrounding 118-row slice census is honestly bounded (completeness claimed only over slice S, singular exclusions logged) and does not need to decide N_q(2) or complete a general classification to preserve the headline witnesses' value.
